field-ReportID:
A unique identifier for this report (e.g., CFP-2025-001).
Create using: Year + sequential number. Coordinate with: Quality/Documentation manager
field-ReportDate:
Date when the report is finalized and issued.
Decide with: Management when report should be published
field-ReportingPeriodStart:
Start date of the period covered by this report (e.g., 2024-01-01).
Must match the timeframe of primary data collection. Ask: Production/Facilities manager for data collection period
field-ReportingPeriodEnd:
End date of the period covered by this report (e.g., 2024-12-31).
Should align with fiscal year or data availability. Coordinate with: Finance/Management team
field-OrganizationName:
Your company's legal registered name.
Check: Legal department, company registration documents, or official letterhead
field-OrganizationAddress:
Registered address (city, country).
Get from: Legal/HR department, company registration documents
field-ProductName:
Commercial name customers know your product by.
Ask: Marketing/Product Manager
field-DeclaredUnit:
Unit for reporting results (e.g., "1 piece", "1 kg", "1 liter").
Ask: Product/Technical manager
field-ProductDescription:
Brief description of what the product is and its key features.
Ask: Marketing/Product Manager or Technical team
field-StudyGoal:
Why you're doing this study (e.g., "customer requirements", "eco-labeling", "internal improvement").
Decide with: Management/Sustainability team
field-IntendedAudience:
Who will use this report (e.g., "customers", "internal team", "regulators").
Decide with: Management
field-SystemBoundaryType:
Boundary type: Use "CradleToGrave" (full lifecycle) or "CradleToGate" (until factory gate).
Decide with: Management
field-Applications:
Applications is MultiEnum.
Example: FootprintCommunication; DesignImprovement
field-CFPType:
Type: Use "FullCFP" for complete study, "CommunicationCFP" for simplified external communication.
Decide with: Management based on report purpose
field-ImpactCategory:
Always "Climate change (GWP)" for carbon footprint studies.
Confirm with: Quality/Technical team
field-LifeCycleStagesIncluded:
Which stages: RawMaterial; Production; Distribution; Use; EndOfLife.
Decide with: Management and check what data you can realistically collect
field-AllocationApproach:
How to split impacts between co-products: Use "Mass" (by weight) as default if you make multiple products.
Ask: Production manager about co-products
field-CutOffCriteria:
Rules for excluding minor inputs (e.g., "<1% mass and energy").
Use standard approach; confirm with: Management if specific criteria needed
field-KeyAssumptions:
Major assumptions made in the study (e.g., product lifetime, usage patterns, recycling rates).
Ask: Product manager for lifetime expectations; Marketing for usage patterns; Industry association for typical values
field-ElectricityMixSelectionMethod:
How electricity data was chosen.
Write "Location-based regional grid mix for [your country/region]"; get country info from: Facilities manager
field-DataCollectionApproach:
How you collected data.
Write summary coordinating with: Production manager, Procurement team, Facilities manager about their data sources
field-DataQualityRequirements:
Target quality for data.
Write standard text; confirm requirements with: Quality/Management team
field-ImpactAssessmentMethod:
Method for calculating global warming potential.
Recommended: "IPCC AR6 GWP 100" (latest standard). AR5/AR4 for comparability with older studies. GTP for temperature-based metric. Confirm with: Quality/Technical team
field-GHGsIncluded:
Greenhouse gases included in calculations.
Minimum (ISO 14067): "CO2; CH4; N2O" (carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide).
Complete Kyoto Protocol: "CO2; CH4; N2O; HFCs; PFCs; SF6; NF3"
Confirm with: Quality/Technical team based on your industry sector
field-GWPTimeHorizonYears:
Time horizon for GWP characterization.
Standard: "100" years (most common, allows comparability).
20 years: short-term climate impact.
500 years: long-term perspective.
Confirm with: Quality team if different timeframe needed
field-TotalCFP_CO2e:
Total carbon footprint result in kg CO2 equivalent.
Calculate: Sum of all life cycle stages. Use CarbonSig calculation engine
field-UncertaintyRange_CO2e:
Uncertainty range for total CFP (e.g., 1.70–2.05).
Calculate from: Uncertainty analysis (Monte Carlo or sensitivity analysis). Coordinate with: Technical team
field-StageResults_RawMaterial_CO2e:
Carbon impact from raw materials.
Get material weights from: Production manager. Get emission factors from: Procurement (ask suppliers for environmental data) or use EPA/government databases
field-StageResults_Production_CO2e:
Carbon impact from manufacturing.
Get energy usage from: Facilities manager, Production manager. Get emission factors from: Utility bills or energy supplier
field-StageResults_Distribution_CO2e:
Carbon impact from transport/distribution.
Get distances from: Logistics manager. Get vehicle types from: Transport coordinator. Use government transport emission factors
field-StageResults_Use_CO2e:
Carbon impact during product use.
Get usage patterns from: Marketing, Customer service. Get energy consumption from: Product specifications (ask R&D/Technical team)
field-StageResults_EndOfLife_CO2e:
Carbon impact from disposal/recycling.
Use waste percentages from above + government waste emission factors. Ask: Facilities manager about disposal methods
field-DirectEmissionsCO2Fossil:
Direct fossil-based CO2 emissions from production processes (kg CO2e).
ISO 14067 requires separate reporting of fossil vs biogenic carbon. Get from: Process data, combustion calculations. Ask: Production manager about fuel consumption
field-BiogenicCO2Emissions_CO2e:
CO2 emissions from biogenic sources (kg CO2e).
Biogenic carbon from biomass, wood, agricultural products. Must be reported separately per ISO 14067. Get from: Material composition analysis. Ask: Procurement about bio-based materials
field-BiogenicCO2Uptake_CO2e:
CO2 absorbed during biomass growth (kg CO2e, negative value).
Carbon sequestered during plant/tree growth. Report as negative number. Calculate based on: Biomass carbon content. Coordinate with: Sustainability team or LCA specialist
field-HotspotsSummary:
Short narrative of main emission drivers (hotspots).
Analyze: Results breakdown by stage. Identify: Top 3 emission contributors. Write: 2-3 sentence summary
field-Limitations:
Study limitations.
Document with: Each department what data they couldn't provide; note time/budget constraints; list areas where estimates were used
field-Conclusions:
Key findings from the study.
Analyze results with: Finance team (cost implications); Production manager (improvement opportunities); summarize which life cycle stage has highest impact
field-Recommendations:
Suggestions for improvement.
Develop with: Production manager (process changes); Procurement (supplier alternatives); Management (investment decisions); focus on largest impact areas
field-IntendedCommunicationMode:
How results will be shared: Public; B2B; Internal; etc.
Decide with: Marketing, Management
field-ComparativeAssertionPublic:
Whether you'll compare publicly with competitors (true/false).
Decide with: Marketing/Legal team
field-ComparativeAssertionRulesFollowed: Rules/standards followed if comparative (ISO 14044, PCR, etc.).
field-PrimaryDataSources:
Your company's direct data sources (e.g., "plant meter readings; procurement records").
Ask: Production manager, Purchasing, Facilities
field-BackgroundDataSets:
External databases used.
Ask: IT/Research team to help find free government databases (EPA, energy ministries). Request from: Procurement team for supplier environmental data
field-ElectricityGridMix:
Electricity grid data source for your region.
Check: Utility bills for supplier info; ask Facilities manager for energy contracts; search national grid operator websites
field-EmissionFactorsList:
Source of emission factors used.
Document sources found with help from: IT/Research team for database access; Procurement for supplier data
field-AuthorName:
Who prepared the report.
Usually: Environmental consultant or you
field-ApproverName:
Manager who approves the report.
Ask: Your supervisor
field-ChangeLog: Brief list of changes between versions.
materialsTable:
Add all materials and components used in your product.
Ask: Production manager for bill of materials (BOM); Procurement team for material specifications; R&D for component details
energyTable:
Add all energy inputs during production.
Ask: Facilities manager for electricity/gas meter readings; Production manager for machine-specific energy use; Utility bills for consumption data
outputsTable:
Add co-products and outputs from production.
Ask: Production manager about by-products; Quality team about scrap/waste streams; Sales about co-products sold
wasteTable:
Add waste streams generated during production.
Ask: Facilities manager about waste disposal contracts; Environmental manager about waste tracking; Production manager about scrap percentages
transportTable:
Add all transportation stages (inbound materials, outbound distribution).
Ask: Logistics manager for shipping routes; Procurement for supplier locations; Sales for distribution network; Transport coordinator for vehicle types
useTable:
Add typical use scenarios for your product.
Ask: Marketing for customer usage patterns; Customer service for feedback data; Product manager for design assumptions; R&D for lab test results
eolTable:
Add end-of-life disposal scenarios.
Ask: Environmental manager for waste management data; Industry association for typical disposal rates; Municipal authorities for regional recycling infrastructure
reviewTable:
Add critical reviewers if external review was performed.
Ask: Management if review is required; Quality team about reviewer selection; Certification body for approved reviewers
field-FunctionalUnitDefinition:
A clear description of the quantified performance that the product delivers.
Ask: Product manager or Technical team about main product function. Example: 'Transport and consume 750 mL of beverage per use' or 'Cleaning 1 kg of laundry at 40°C'
field-FunctionalUnitQuantity:
Quantity of functional units (typically 1).
Use: 1 as default unless comparing multiple units
field-ReferenceFlowDescription:
Physical product that delivers the functional unit.
Ask: Technical team. Example: '1 unit of reusable bottle delivered to customer' or '50g of detergent powder'
field-SystemBoundaryDescription:
Detailed textual description of what is included and excluded from the system boundary.
Describe: Which life cycle stages are covered, which processes are included/excluded, and rationale for exclusions. Coordinate with: Technical team and Management to define study scope
field-GeographicalBoundary:
Geographic scope where data applies.
Ask: Sales/Logistics about main markets; use 'EU average' or specific country codes
field-TemporalBoundary:
Time period for data collection.
Check: When primary data collected (ask Production manager); When background databases dated (usually 2019-2023)
field-TechnologicalBoundary:
Key technologies used in production.
Ask: Production manager about main manufacturing processes. Example: 'Electric arc furnace steel; injection molding cap'
field-RepresentativenessGeographical:
How well data matches geographic scope (High/Medium/Low).
Decide: High if site-specific data in target region; Medium if regional average; Low if global proxy data
field-RepresentativenessTemporal:
How recent the data is (High/Medium/Low).
Decide: High if <3 years old; Medium if 3-5 years; Low if >5 years
field-RepresentativenessTechnological:
How well data matches actual technology (High/Medium/Low).
Decide: High if exact process data; Medium if similar technology; Low if generic proxy
field-Completeness:
Coverage of processes and flows (High/Medium/Low).
Decide with: Quality team based on cut-off criteria and data gaps
field-Consistency:
Uniformity of methods across study (High/Medium/Low).
Decide with: Quality team if same calculation methods used throughout
field-Reliability:
Source verification and validation (High/Medium/Low).
Decide: High if audited/certified data; Medium if supplier declarations; Low if estimates
field-Precision:
Accuracy and detail of measurements (High/Medium/Low).
Decide: High if precise measurements with calibrated instruments; Medium if standard measurements; Low if estimates/approximations. Ask: Production manager about measurement precision
field-DataQualityAssessmentMethod:
Method used to evaluate data quality.
Examples: 'DQI matrix based on pedigree scores', 'Semi-quantitative pedigree approach per ecoinvent guidelines', 'Qualitative expert judgment'. Coordinate with: Quality/Technical team for standardized approach
field-PCRReference:
Product Category Rules document reference, if applicable.
Check: Industry association or certification body websites for relevant PCR documents. Leave empty if no specific PCR used
field-Version:
Version number of this report.
Use: '1.0' for first release; increment for updates (1.1, 2.0, etc.). Coordinate with: Quality/Documentation manager
field-PreviousVersions:
List of previous version numbers and dates.
Example: '0.9 (draft, 2024-08-15); 1.0 (approved, 2025-01-10)'. Track with: Documentation manager
field-ProductIdentifier:
Internal product code or SKU.
Get from: Product database, ERP system. Ask: Product manager or IT department
field-IntendedUse:
Primary purpose of the product.
Ask: Marketing/Product manager. Example: 'Reusable drink container', 'Industrial cleaning agent'
field-ProductCategoryClassification:
Industry classification code (e.g., CPC, NACE).
Check: Industry standards or certification requirements. Ask: Quality team or industry association
field-Market:
Target markets for this product.
Ask: Sales/Marketing team. Example: 'EU; US; Asia-Pacific'
field-VariantsCovered:
Product variants included in this study.
Ask: Product manager about SKU variations. Example: 'Blue 750 mL; Black 750 mL; Red 750 mL'
field-AverageProductMass:
Average mass of the product in kilograms.
Get from: Product specifications, Bill of Materials. Ask: Production manager or Technical team
field-OffsetsUsed:
Whether carbon offsets were purchased to neutralize emissions (Yes/No).
Ask: Sustainability team or Finance department if offsets purchased
field-OffsetProjectIDs:
Unique identifiers of offset projects used.
Get from: Offset provider certificates. Example: 'VCS-1234; GS-5678'. Ask: Sustainability team or Finance for offset purchase documentation
field-OffsetStandards:
Certification standards for offsets.
Check: Offset certificates for standards used. Common: 'Verified Carbon Standard (VCS)', 'Gold Standard', 'Climate Action Reserve'
field-ResidualEmissionsAfterOffsets:
Remaining emissions after applying offsets (kg CO2e).
Calculate: Total CFP minus offset amount. Coordinate with: Finance/Sustainability team
field-CommunicationClaims:
Specific claims being made publicly about the carbon footprint.
Develop with: Marketing and Legal teams. Must be accurate, verifiable, and not misleading per ISO 14021
field-LabelingProgram:
Carbon labeling program enrolled in, if any.
Check: If participating in Carbon Trust label, CarbonNeutral certification, etc. Ask: Marketing/Sustainability team
field-CommunicationCompliance:
Whether communication follows ISO 14021 and ISO 14067 requirements (Yes/No).
Verify with: Legal/Compliance team that all claims are substantiated and meet standard requirements
field-VerificationPerformed:
Whether third-party verification was conducted (Yes/No).
Ask: Management if external verification body was hired. Different from critical review - this is formal verification per ISO 14064-3
field-VerificationBody:
Name of independent verification organization.
Get from: Verification contract or certificate. Example: 'Bureau Veritas', 'DNV', 'TÜV Rheinland'
field-VerificationStandard:
Standard(s) used for verification.
Check: Verification statement for standards. Common: 'ISO 14064-3:2019', 'ISO 14065:2020'
field-VerificationDate:
Date when verification was completed.
Get from: Verification statement or certificate
field-VerificationStatementLink:
URL or path to verification statement document.
Get from: Quality/Documentation team. Should be accessible to report users
field-UsePhaseEmissionsCO2e:
Total aggregated emissions from all use phase scenarios (kg CO2e).
Sum of energy consumption and maintenance activities over product lifetime. Calculate based on: Use scenarios table above. Ask: Product manager for typical usage patterns; R&D for energy consumption data
